bullets.title: NVDA CEO Jensen Huang reinstated; Trump backing clears national security overhang
bullets.body: NVIDIA's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as President, CEO, and board director effective immediately, following input from senior U.S. government officials including Trump, who stated the move poses no national security risk. Shares surged ~24-29% pre-market, with Citi raising PT to $240 (15x FY28E EPS) and Melius/Bernstein upgrading to Buy with $200-220 PTs. Remaining overhangs: ongoing foreign intelligence investigation, Megaspeed export probes, delayed 10-Q, and upcoming congressional interviews.

bullets.title: Market staging sharp bounce after worst week since 2001; tactical but sustainability uncertain
bullets.body: S&P 500 futures jumped +4.3%, Nasdaq +6.9% Monday after the SPX fell 8.6% and SOX dropped 17.1% last week—the worst NASDAQ decline since March 2020. MS strategist Wilson calls this 'The Fat Pitch' with SPX trading ~16.4x vs 19-19.6x fair value, NDX below COVID trough. VIX hit 35.9, Goldman Panic Index a record 9.8, HF net exposure at 42% (8th percentile since 2010), and 14-day RSI at 24.69 (most oversold since taper tantrum)—but GS cautions a durable bottom requires improved AI monetization, more dovish Fed, or deeper positioning washout.

bullets.title: AI CapEx deceleration is the core macro risk; Goldman sees earnings impulse fading in 2027
bullets.body: Goldman notes AI infrastructure drove ~50% of S&P 500 earnings growth in 2026 and ~67% of expected 2027 growth, but the earnings impulse is set to fade as CapEx decelerates. JPMorgan turns tactically cautious, framing this as 'AI Capex 3.0'—growth rates decelerating as capital becomes the constraint. Asia investors are debating outright 2027 capex cuts (not just moderation), putting DELL/STX/WDC server valuations under pressure near historical troughs.

bullets.title: Fed not pivoting: equity rally would push yields higher, keeping financial conditions flat
bullets.body: 22V and others flag that financial conditions tightened 18bps last week and remain near neutral; the Fed is comfortable keeping FCI flat until growth/inflation slow. If equities rally, rising 10Y yields (currently 4.97%) will likely offset the easing, precluding a sustainable 'everything rally.' Market now fully prices two Fed hikes by March; a durable bottom requires a more dovish Fed signal, seen as low-odds through early 2027. Treasury Secretary Bessent separately warned the Fed risks overtightening.

bullets.title: November flash PMIs: US manufacturing and services soften but remain expansionary
bullets.body: US Manufacturing PMI edged to 53.3-54.5 (down 0.4 pts) with output and employment growth slowing, though new orders ticked up. Services PMI slipped to 54.7 with drops in new orders and employment. Morgan Stanley cut its ISM Manufacturing PMI tracking estimate to 54.7 from 55.5. Input/output prices both dropped ~1pp; vendor delivery times lengthened, likely from war-related supply-chain disruptions.

bullets.title: Eurozone PMIs bifurcated; ECB expected to hike Dec 17
bullets.body: Eurozone composite PMI held flat at 51.7% in November with manufacturing rising and services declining; Germany outperforming while France contracted more than expected. Models project manufacturing PMI slipping from 52.9% to 50.8% by Sep 2027. The ECB is expected to hike on Dec 17 with at least one more hike this cycle; France's OAT yield above nominal GDP growth acts as an activity headwind.

bullets.title: CRWD acquires Zscaler for ~$44B all-stock, creating $10B+ ARR cybersecurity platform
bullets.body: CrowdStrike is acquiring Zscaler in an all-stock deal valued at ~$43.9B (34% premium), with CRWD shareholders retaining 84.1% of the combined entity. The deal targets ~$1B annualized revenue synergies by 30 months post-close and ~$500M cost synergies within 18-24 months; combined ARR exceeds $10B. Low horizontal antitrust risk expected given complementary endpoint (CRWD) vs. network-level (ZS) security approaches; HSR filing due by Jan 5, 2027, with May 2027 target close.

bullets.title: HF positioning near capitulation but not there yet; crowding at record highs
bullets.body: GS notes hedge fund net exposure is at its lowest since April 2025 (39% L/S net leverage) with futures length still in the 82nd percentile, and the crowding index at a record high with the median HF holding 70% of its long book in the top 10 positions. CTAs flipped net short $19B after selling $57B in the past month. GS prefers defensives and buyback aristocrats; shared HF favorites include APH, COF, MA, SPCX, SPOT, UNH, V.

bullets.title: UBS semis analyst cutting data center estimates; aligning with lower production scenario
bullets.body: UBS semiconductor analyst Tim Arcuri is hosting a midday call to cut data center estimates across coverage, aligning with LPS guidance. The broader thesis from UBS: semiconductor investors are capitulating to the view that the supply chain overbuilt relative to demand, with a flatter GW profile expected in C2027-C2028; MU at ~$325 (~2x TBV) seen as a possible 'AI trade is over' signal with the market pricing two-thirds of the way to that scenario.

bullets.title: Cross-asset signals needed to confirm AI rally is real: yields, curve, commodities, dollar
bullets.body: OPCO flags that NVDA is up 29% on Jensen's return but hedge fund positioning in the 0th percentile provides upside fuel only if cross-asset confirms—specifically yields rising, the curve steepening, commodities rallying, and the dollar selling off. SPX faces technical resistance at 7,300-7,400 (200-day MA) with negative gamma into 7,300. The 2018 Q4 analog suggests the market only bottomed once the Fed pivoted.

bullets.title: US CPI tracking 3.8% YoY in November; disinflation progress slow
bullets.body: JPMorgan's monthly inflation forecasts show US headline CPI at 3.8% YoY in November (down from 4.0% in October) and PCE at 3.7% (down from 3.8%). Core CPI is tracking 2.9% YoY—still well above the Fed's 2% target. Japan CPI is rising (2.8% headline), and global ex-China/Turkey headline stands at 3.9%.

bullets.title: AI risk spreading into financial services; 'Trust Infrastructure' vs 'Trust Dependent' bifurcation
bullets.body: 22V identifies a regime shift where AI risk is spreading across Financial Services: Trust Infrastructure names (exchanges, data vendors, payments rails) benefit while Trust Dependent names (lenders, brokers) are hurt. A long Trust Infrastructure / short Trust Dependent strategy gained 18.9% since Meta's Muse release with 0.61 correlation to HY CDX. The flatter yield curve (2/10 at ~30bps) also disproportionately pressures banks.

bullets.title: Data center backlash drives distributed/onsite power as new infrastructure theme
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley names BE and SEI top picks in distributed power as data center political backlash from midterms elevates bring-your-own-power (BYOP) adoption. US data center power demand through 2029 is ~185 GW gross with a ~74 GW shortfall; political scrutiny could delay ~5 GW of capacity from 2028 into 2029. SOFCs rank #1 in a composite scorecard (4.5/5) on emissions and noise, factors expected to carry greater weight in the current environment.

bullets.title: Agentic commerce: Walmart leading, Amazon cautious; Mizuho upgrades WMT
bullets.body: Mizuho upgrades WMT to Outperform ($135 PT, 38x FY28E) as Walmart's Muse+Sparky agent-to-agent integration goes live ahead of Cyber 5, positioning it as the primary agentic commerce play. Amazon CEO Jassy has taken a guarded approach to opening its platform to third-party agents—seen as a competitive disadvantage in the near term.

bullets.title: Goldman macro overlay: prefer long US 5Y rates and buyback aristocrats over AI mega-caps
bullets.body: Goldman's Marquee Macro Overlay recommends long US 5-year rates (3m/5y USD receiver) as its preferred macro trade, and buyback aristocrats as the next earnings leadership phase as growth broadens beyond AI names. The AI correction has improved valuations and risk premia but positioning and macro-stress indicators have not reached unambiguous buy levels.

bullets.title: AMZN acquires Decart AI for ~$7.5B to advance custom silicon and inference efficiency
bullets.body: Amazon confirmed an agreement to acquire Decart's proprietary Optimization Stack (DOS) technology with the co-founders and research team joining Amazon, targeting custom silicon and AI inference advancement. The FT reported a ~$7.5B price; transaction is subject to regulatory clearance. The deal is framed as a competitive move against NVDA's inference dominance.

bullets.title: Staples vs. Tech rotation most extreme since the dot-com bust; Black Friday risk skews lower
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes Staples outperformed Tech by 49% in under two months—the biggest such rotation since the TMT bubble unwind in March 2001—and Staples now trade at a 73% PE premium to IT globally, the largest ever by >30 percentage points. Black Friday preview is cautious: retailers face strong prior-year comparisons, softer recent trends, and increased discounting with downside risk after the sector rally.

bullets.title: European macro: China trade shock and AI gap widen; ECB hike cycle adds pressure
bullets.body: JPMorgan's Joyce Chang highlights that China now competes directly with the eurozone in ~40% of sectors where Europe holds comparative advantage (up from 25% in the early 2000s), and Europe's AI edge lies in applications not requiring frontier models. Growing hedge fund ownership of sovereign debt creates a more price-sensitive marginal buyer, reducing tolerance for fiscal slippage; France and the US require the largest fiscal adjustments among peers.

bullets.title: Meta raises Opex to $227B on cloud spend; 2027/2028 EPS cut 13%/11%
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley cuts META estimates as the company raises Opex guidance to $227B driven by cloud/AI infrastructure spend, resulting in 2027 EPS cut of 13% and 2028 EPS cut of 11%; PT lowered to $720. Separately, MS is tracking Gemini 4 Hydrogen at ~4X efficiency improvement over Gemini 3.8 Flash as the GOOGL vs META agentic model multiplier comparison becomes a key 2027 investment debate.

bullets.title: Weekly M&A wave: CRWD/ZS $44B, PANW/Applied Compute $4.5B, AMZN/Decart $7.5B, INTU sells Mailchimp for $3.68B
bullets.body: The week of Nov 16-22 saw a surge of tech M&A: CRWD acquiring ZS (~$44B all-stock), PANW buying Applied Compute for $4.5B in stock, Amazon near a $7.5B deal for Decart, and Bending Spoons acquiring Mailchimp from Intuit at ~$3.68B EV. Additional deals include BILL acquired by TPG/Corpay at $63.25/sh and GTCR considering a buyout of GPN.
